# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

I changed nothing; this is all from reading the code. The main thing to know first: **the due arithmetic is written three times.** The screen works out every money figure itself in TypeScript. The server works out the same figures again in Java (`ClaimRepository`) for the audit, statements, period closes, settling and the permission thresholds. A third Java copy (`SheetAsOf`) handles statements taken "as of" a past date. --- ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Claim row (`claims.slot.tsx`) | Figure (`data-testid`) | Rule | |---|---| | `claim-number` | Given when a DRAFT is **opened**, not when it is created. Sheet-wide 1, 2, 3… (`ClaimRepository.number`). With period numbering on (`numbersPerPeriod`: a period-numbering from-date is set and today is on or after it), it is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by is in no period (`numberInPeriod`). A rejected claim keeps its number, and so does a voided one (never reused). A split-off claim gets a new number. | | `claim-amount` | Two decimals. A negative amount is a **correction**: it must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person, and only a negative amount may name one (`ClaimInput.checkCorrection`). | | `claim-date` | A blank date takes the sheet's **entry date**, or today when none is set, on add, paste and quick-add (`SheetRepository.entryDate`). On editing a draft, a blank date takes **today** instead (`SaveClaim`). That is an inconsistency. | | `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is created (`ClaimRepository.dueBy`): the *terms*-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays. Terms come from the person's own terms, else the grade's `terms-` in force on the date, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). Editing a draft's date re-fixes it (`SaveClaim`). Adding a holiday re-fixes it for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday (`refixDueBy`). Re-dating a claim does **not** change it. | | `claim-period` | The period containing the **due-by**, not the claim's date (`periodOf`). | | `claim-due` | `claimDueNow` (TS), which mirrors `ClaimRepository.dueNow`. Worked through in the next section. | | `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue`: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and its **overdue-from** day is before today. Overdue-from = due-by + `grace-` days (calendar days), using the grade the person had on the claim's date and the grace in force then. | | `claim-stated` | The raw `stated` flag. Note that "bound" also needs the claim not to be PENDING (`Claim.bound`). | | `claim-deferred` / `-until` | Deferred = status OPEN and `deferredUntil` is after today. You can only defer an OPEN claim, to a date after today, and not in a closed period. A deferred claim counts in no total, is never overdue, cannot be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound. | | `claim-late-entry` | Set when the claim is added and its due-by falls in a **soft-closed** period (`lateEntry`). It also writes a `LATE_ENTRY` audit line. | | `claim-status` | DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED. A clerk settling above the limit sends it to PENDING; a steward then approves (SETTLED) or rejects (back to OPEN). DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims can be voided. Rules are below. | | `claim-batch`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-log`, `claim-comments` | Stored values. Reminding is allowed once per "today", for OPEN or PENDING claims only. A proof can be added unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID, or in a closed period. Each log line records the due as computed on the server at that moment. | ### How a claim's due is worked out (`dueNow` / `claimDueNow`) 1. **Settled:** the due frozen at settlement (`settled_due`) is shown as is. 2. **Otherwise the claim needs a figure** (`figure`): - A bound statement figure is used, or `n/a` when the statement bound it to n/a. - Else the **live rate figure** (`due`): amount × rate ÷ 100. - Rate = the rate of the grade the person had **on the claim's date**, using the rate with the latest from-date on or before that date. An undated rate applies from the beginning of time. - There is no figure (`n/a`) when that rate's to-date is before the claim's date. 3. **Rounding** (`rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): - Half up when the claim is dated before the sheet's **policy date** (a blank policy date means today). Otherwise half to even. - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. 4. **Late charge** (`lateCharge` / `withCharge`), only while overdue: - For every full 30 days past overdue-from, apply the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary. - Each charge is taken on figure + earlier charges (it **compounds**) and is rounded on its own. - A statement never binds the charge; it keeps growing with today until settlement freezes it. 5. **Floor:** the result is at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). 6. **Corrections** (negative amounts) get no floor and no late charge. ### Which claims count (`Claim.counts` / `counts`) - A claim counts if it is **SETTLED**, or if it is **OPEN/PENDING**, not deferred, and either bound by a statement or not dated inside one of the person's **holds**. - **Retirement:** once today is on or after the retirement date, the person is treated as held over every date (`liveHolds` / `holdsById`). Their unbound open claims then drop out of all live totals. - **For periods** (`countsAs` / `countsOn`): a claim counts by the status its log shows at the end of the period's last day. Holds only remove claims that are still open now. ### Person row | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `person-claimed` | Sum of the **amounts** of counting claims. The TS version adds them with floating-point `Number` math; everything else uses exact cents. | | `person-due-total` | Sum of `dueNow` over counting claims, skipping `n/a`, held to the **cap** in force on today. It shows `n/a` only when no rate for the person's grade is in force today **and** no counting claim has a fixed figure or a due. | | `person-excess` | How far the uncapped sum is above the cap, else 0.00. | | `person-settled-total` / `-open-total` | The uncapped due-total split by SETTLED vs OPEN/PENDING. | | `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | Counting claims that are overdue, and the sum of their dues. | | `person-aged-0-30/31-60/61` | Dues of counting OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by days since the claim's date (frontend only). | | `person-active` | Has a counting open claim dated within the last 30 days, today included (frontend only). | | `person-period-

-due-total` | Open period: dues of counting claims whose **due-by** falls in the period. Closed or soft-closed: the per-person total frozen at close (0.00 for anyone added since). | | `person-statement-count`, `-stated-total`, `-statement-date` | Set by taking a statement (below). | | `person-backing` | Frozen dues of the person's patrons' SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days. | | `person-grade` | The grade in force on today: the one with the latest from-date on or before it. The first grade applies from the beginning of time. A save that leaves the grade unchanged with a blank from-date records no new grade. | ### Sheet-level figures - **`rollup-due-total`, `header-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `header-overdue-total`** use `trimmedSum`: people's figures added up, leaving out the single highest and lowest when three or more people have one. The server's `Rollup.trimmed` does the same for the audit. - **`rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-overdue-count`** are plain sums. - **`summary-grade--due-total`** is a plain sum of the capped person totals, with retired people left out. **`-count`** and **`-active`** count people the same way. - **Period figures:** - `period-due-total` and `summary-period-*` are the sum of the per-person period totals. - `period-closed` shows yes, soft or no. - **Other totals:** - `month-*-due-total` groups counting dues by the claim's **date** month. - `tag-*-due-total` groups them by tag; a claim with two tags counts in both. - `header-claims-*-count` and `summary-status-*` count claims by status. - `summary-void-*` counts VOID claims by void reason. - **Rates:** - `rate-current-` is the grade's rate in force today, or `n/a`. - `rate-preview-count` and `-diff` are frontend only.
